title: Article 327 — Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections to Legislatures

content.overview: Article 327 empowers Parliament to from time to time by law make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State, including the preparation of electoral rolls, the delimitation of constituencies and all other matters necessary for securing the due constitution of such House or Houses.
content.glance: Parliament may by law provide for all matters relating to elections to Parliament and State Legislatures (rolls, delimitation, due constitution).
content.study:
Article 327 is the principal parliamentary power over election law for Parliament and State Legislatures. It supports the Representation of the People Acts, delimitation law, and related statutes. Subject to the Constitution (including Arts 324–326 and 329).

Examination: plenary parliamentary power on election matters; includes rolls and delimitation; link Art 328 (State supplemental power).

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may by law make provision for all matters relating to elections to Parliament and State Legislatures, including electoral rolls, delimitation of constituencies, and securing due constitution of the Houses.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What power does Parliament have under Article 327?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 327, Parliament may from time to time by law make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State, including the preparation of electoral rolls, the delimitation of constituencies and all other matters necessary for securing the due constitution of such House or Houses.
